title: sed-guard: sed modifies files directly, prefer wkedit
desc: Warns when sed -i or sed redirect modifies source files. wkedit is the safe alternative with UTF-8 and encoding guarantees.
steps: SAFETY: Catches 'sed -i' or 'sed ... > file.ext' on source files (ps1, sh, py, cs, md, json, txt). sed bypasses UTF-8 encoding enforcement, skips backup creation, and can corrupt files on CRLF/LF mixed endings or multibyte characters.
SOLUTION: Use 'wkedit' instead: wkedit.sh --old-file old.txt --new-file new.txt target.file. wkedit creates a .bak backup, preserves encoding, and is harness-safe.
PREVENTION: Never use sed -i on repository source files. Use wkedit for any file replacement that touches source code or configuration. wkedit handles encoding, backup, and diff display correctly.
author: claude
